maria: Quick question — I'm wiring up a background job in our staging container that needs to call the CLI non-interactively. What's the recommended pattern for handing off auth tokens to ephemeral CI containers without using interactive browser auth?

sam: We usually do one of two things: 1) short-lived token file mounted into the container (with strict perms) or 2) env var injection for ephemeral jobs. Avoid long-lived tokens in image layers.

eli: For systemd/docker services I prefer a token file under /run/secrets/redwood_profile (readonly to the service user). That way it disappears on reboot. Example: use a small init step that writes the file and starts the worker 

jason: If you go env var route, use REDWOOD_TOKEN (process env) + REDWOOD_PROFILE to select any profile-specific overrides. Also ensure the token has a short TTL and rotation logic in the parent process.

maria: Any concrete commands/config I can copy-paste? I'm trying to keep it noninteractive and inside a simple shell script.

sam: Paste this as a template — adapt as needed.

```
# write token into an ephemeral file (CI secret injected at runtime)
mkdir -p /run/redwood && chmod 700 /run/redwood
cat > /run/redwood/ci_token <<'EOF'
sk_live_token_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
EOF
chmod 600 /run/redwood/ci_token
# export for the child process
export REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE=/run/redwood/ci_token
# example invocation the worker reads file and sets env for the CLI
export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat $REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE)
redwood-cli jobs run --noninteractive --profile ci
```

eli: For systemd unit files you can add `ProtectHome=yes` and `ReadOnlyDirectories=/run/redwood` and drop privileges to a service user. Keeps the surface small.

jason: Small gotcha: node SDK streaming currently needs `--stream` flag on the CLI side to keep chunking behavior consistent; without it some wrapper libraries will buffer until EOF. Python client is fine but ensure you call `client.stream()` rather than the sync API.

maria: Good to know. Anything about retries/timeouts for background jobs?

sam: Use exponential backoff on 429/5xx. We generally implement: initial=200ms, factor=2, max=10s, attempts=6. Also treat 401/403 as terminal (trigger reauth).

jason: And when using file-based tokens, watch out for stale TTLs — add a small TTL-check at startup: if token expiry < now+30s, fail fast so orchestrator can rotate.

eli: If your orchestrator can't rotate, consider a tiny sidecar that refreshes tokens via a privileged service account and writes to /run/redwood. That keeps worker code simple.

devex-bot: Docs update: https://internal.redwood.dev/docs/cli-auth#ephemeral-containers (added sample systemd + docker examples) :sparkles:

maria: Perfect, I'll try the file-mount approach with TTL-check and report back. Thanks! :pray:
